content: 1. Establish a standardized set of national HIV indicators, selecting from the 18 key indicators outlined in the guidelines, while considering the stage of transition to the treat all approach. Any additional indicators should be chosen from the 2015 Consolidated Strategic Information Guidelines and must be strongly justified for their inclusion. 2. Adopt and adapt the generic tools and recommendations for HIV patient monitoring and case surveillance from the WHO Consolidated Guidelines on person-centered HIV patient monitoring. These tools should be customized to the specific context of each country and program to ensure the delivery of essential, high-quality patient care. 3. Update and standardize minimum datasets and tools, both paper-based and electronic, for patient monitoring. This includes revising core paper-based tools such as HIV patient cards, antiretroviral therapy (ART) registers, and cross-sectional and cohort reports. 4. Develop or update ART community monitoring tools, transfer/referral forms, patient-held cards, and appointment books as necessary. 5. Revise HIV data elements in maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH), tuberculosis (TB), and other relevant program monitoring tools to ensure integration and consistency. 6. Update data elements in electronic medical records, registers, and reporting systems to align with current needs and standards. 7. Implement a tiered approach to transitioning patient monitoring data from paper-based tools to electronic systems, based on resource availability, site capacity, and specific settings. 8. Harmonize HIV data elements, patient monitoring tools, and indicators across facilities and programs, including TB, MNCH, and other service areas, to ensure consistency and integration. 9. Use HIV patient cards and ART registers at TB and MNCH sites to facilitate integrated service delivery and data collection. 10. Integrate HIV data into the Health Management Information System (HMIS) and collaborate with other national programs and external institutions to enhance data sharing and program efficiency. 11. Conduct periodic reviews (every six months or annually) of patient monitoring data to assess data quality and collect additional key indicators as needed. 12. Improve national and global reporting by simplifying disaggregation categories, standardizing reporting forms and tally tools, and establishing regular feedback loops. 13. Allow lay health workers to collect and report data to reduce the workload on clinical staff, while ensuring data quality and accuracy. 14. Strengthen routine clinical mentoring and supportive supervision to maintain high standards of care and data quality. 15. Use available data to develop dashboards and other tools to identify gaps in the quality of care and address them through routine analysis and periodic review processes. 16. Ensure that an HIV patient card is created for every individual enrolled in HIV care, regardless of the service delivery point. 17. Assign or develop unique patient identifiers and use appointment systems or linked pharmacy and clinical records to track and follow up with patients who miss appointments. 18. Utilize patient-held cards or passports and transfer/referral forms to facilitate the tracking of patients across different service delivery points. 19. Provide evidence of the benefits of patient monitoring data for both patients and programs to ensure the sustainability of improvements. 20. Develop short-, medium-, and long-term plans for the patient monitoring system, incorporating strategic planning and policy documents to guide implementation and sustainability. 21. Ensure the necessary infrastructure for a three-tiered patient monitoring system, including paper-based registers, electronic registers, and networked online systems. This requires proper folder flow, standardized clinical stationery, protected time for data transcription, adequate workspace, electricity, computer equipment, IT strategies to prevent issues like viruses, and stable network facilities. 22. Train personnel in computer skills and provide IT support to ensure efficient data management and system functionality.
